scenes.title: Check the day, time and open needs
scenes.narration_exact: Before joining a shift, read its day detail. This recorded example is Training, Academy signup practice, on Tuesday, October twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six, from one until three in the afternoon. These are historical recording dates; use an eligible day for your own practice. Open slots shows two. Under Open needs, Firehouse fifty-one lists Chief and Needed, two, while Roster says no one is on this day yet. Check that this is the intended occurrence and appropriate work for you, then choose Sign Up.

scenes.title: Choose the team before confirming
scenes.narration_exact: Choose your team explains that you are selecting the group you are signing up with for this day. The example offers Firehouse fifty-one, with Chief, two, and Open, two. Its radio choice is selected. Review the shift date and time again above the team. Back returns from this confirmation without submitting this choice. When the intended team and occurrence are correct, choose Confirm sign-up once.

scenes.title: Verify the returned membership and count
scenes.narration_exact: The returned day detail now says You are on, and Open slots has changed from two to one. Under Roster, Firehouse fifty-one contains Wallace Boden with the You label. Open needs shows Chief and Needed, one. Those are the recorded results of this signup. Read the named roster entry as well as the count so you can distinguish your own membership from another person's place. This example returns a rostered result; it does not demonstrate a supervisor approving a pending request.

scenes.title: Find the withdrawal action on the same day
scenes.narration_exact: The same rostered day offers Withdraw. Check the title, date and hours before using it, especially when a shift name repeats on several days. Request trade is a separate action on this screen; this exercise removes the personal signup instead of asking a colleague to take the shift. Follow your department's coverage arrangements before making that change. Choose Withdraw to review its confirmation.

scenes.title: Apply the same checks to your department
scenes.narration_exact: These checks help community paramedicine and mental health teams plan outreach coverage, search-and-rescue teams fill support shifts, security companies staff posts, wildland contractors coordinate crews, and industrial response teams arrange standby coverage. Fire and EMS departments can use them for station staffing. For each setting, verify the occurrence, team needs, your personal roster state and any required approval process. After a signup or withdrawal, read the actual returned result before planning coverage around it.
